elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits Licensee to terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its convenience-termination right upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The added language requires thirty (30) days' prior written notice from Licensee to Licensor.

elements.element: Upon Customer's convenience termination, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination becomes effective.
elements.evidence: Licensor must "refund pro rata any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination."

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during any committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor has no convenience-termination right during the Initial Period or any renewal or extension term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly grants Licensee a convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires a notice period of at least sixty (60) and no more than ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is thirty (30) days, not a period within the required 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three (3) months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed, so there is no fee exceeding the three-month cap.

elements.element: Any Vendor convenience-termination right may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Licensor has no convenience-termination right during the Initial Period or any renewal or extension term; therefore, no such right is exercisable before the end of a term.

elements.element: Any Vendor convenience termination requires ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause grants Licensor no convenience-termination right at all, so the condition requiring notice for exercise of such a right does not arise.

result.reason: The redline cleanly satisfies every preferred requirement: Licensee receives a 30-day written-notice convenience right, post-termination prepaid fees are refunded pro rata, and Licensor is barred from convenience termination during committed terms. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because the Customer notice period is 30 days rather than 60–90 days. The amendment is narrowly tailored and leaves the existing term, renewal, and breach-termination provisions operative.
